findings.title: Universal servant status against child claims
findings.claim: Every being in the heavens and earth comes to al-Rahman as a servant, making creaturely dependence a creation-wide relation that stands against an exceptional offspring status.
findings.mechanism: The focus quantifier kull covers the beings in the heavens and earth; ati carries coming toward al-Rahman, while abdan states the relation in which each arrives. In 2:116, a child claim is followed by all in the heavens and earth belonging to God; 25:59 identifies al-Rahman as creator of those domains; 21:26 rejects a child claim under the same name and calls the referents honored servants. The promise to servants in 19:61 further places the name in a relation of benefit. These wider triggers return through the focus's totality, arrival, name, and servant-state.
findings.reader_payoff: Servanthood becomes more than a label for one disputed figure: the focus places every being in a creator-creature relation, and the 21:26 connection shows that servant status can coexist with honor.
findings.containment: The focus itself states universal arrival as servants; the child-claim comparison comes from the supplied wider connections. The ownership facet is applied analogically to creaturely dependence, not to human legal slavery. The promise in 19:61 is tied to its stated servants, and the honor in 21:26 to its referents; neither benefit is generalized to every being in the focus.

epistemic.reason: The cross-run publication is trusted and anchored to the four exact focus words. The coming branch has qualified lexical identity, and the wider connection targets supply exact Arabic without target morphology, so the global parallels are bounded to their stated surface relations.
